content.text:
I have a complete picture. Here are my findings.

## Answer

The markdown abstraction is a **Go interface** (the frontend uses `react-markdown` directly with no comparable interface — the real abstraction is on the backend).

### 1. The interface

- **`markdown.Service`** — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:31`
  Defined methods: `ExtractAll`, `ExtractTags`, `ExtractProperties`, `RenderMarkdown`, `RenderHTML`, `GenerateSnippet`, `ValidateContent`, `RenameTag`.

### 2. Concrete implementations

- **`service`** (unexported struct) — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:57-60`. It wraps a `goldmark.Markdown`. This is the **only** implementation of `markdown.Service` and it is the one that executes at runtime.
  - Method implementations live in the same file (e.g. `ExtractAll` at :356, `RenderHTML` at :255, `RenderMarkdown` at :244, `GenerateSnippet` at :264, `ValidateContent` at :348).

There are **no mocks, fakes, no-ops, or alternate implementations** of `markdown.Service`. I searched for mock/fake/stub/noop and for any other type implementing the interface's methods — the only method receivers are on `*service`. Even the test suite constructs the real `service` (see below), so the production implementation runs in tests too.

Note: there is a related but distinct type, `renderer.NewMarkdownRenderer()` (`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/renderer/`), used at `markdown.go:250` and `:451`. That is a goldmark AST `NodeRenderer` (renders AST back to markdown text), an internal helper used by `service.RenderMarkdown` — it does **not** implement `markdown.Service`.

### 3. Where it is constructed

`NewService(...)` is the factory — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:85` (returns `&service{...}` at :110). Call sites:

- **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48-51`** — the real runtime construction, inside `NewAPIV1Service`, built with `WithTagExtension()` and `WithMentionExtension()`, assigned to `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` at :56.
- **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44`** — test harness constructs the same real service (assigned at :52). Not a mock.

The instance is then passed by reference (not re-constructed) into other components:
- **`/bench/repo/server/server.go:85`** — `rss.NewRSSService(..., apiV1Service.MarkdownService)`.

### 4. Components that hold the interface (dependency-injected field/param)

- **`APIV1Service.MarkdownService markdown.Service`** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`. Used in `memo_service.go:108,447`, `memo_mention_helpers.go:32`, `memo_service_webhooks.go:85`.
- **`RSSService.MarkdownService markdown.Service`** — `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go:45` (constructor `NewRSSService` at :58, assigned :62, used `RenderHTML` at :339).
- **`Runner.MarkdownService markdown.Service`** — `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16` (constructor `NewRunner` at :19, used at :52; also the free function `RebuildMemoPayload` at :74 takes `markdownService markdown.Service` as a parameter).

### Summary

The interface `markdown.Service` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:31`) has exactly one concrete implementation, the `service` struct (same file, :57), created only via `markdown.NewService` (:85). The single runtime instance is constructed in `NewAPIV1Service` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48`) and dependency-injected into three holders: `APIV1Service` (v1.go:35), `RSSService` (rss/rss.go:45, wired in `server.go:85`), and the memopayload `Runner` (runner.go:16). No test double implementations exist; the same concrete `service` runs in production and tests.
